questions.question: Explain what 4 times 6 means using groups and using an array, and explain why 6 times 4 gives the same answer.
questions.expected_answer: 4 times 6 means 4 groups of 6, which is 6 plus 6 plus 6 plus 6, giving 24. As an array it is 4 rows of 6 dots. Turning the array on its side gives 6 rows of 4 dots, the same 24 dots, so 6 times 4 is also 24.

questions.question: Describe the pattern in the 9 times table and use it to find 9 times 7.
questions.expected_answer: For 9 times a number up to 10, the tens digit is one less than that number and the digits of the answer add to 9. For 9 times 7, the tens digit is 6 and the units digit is 9 minus 6, which is 3, so 9 times 7 is 63.

questions.question: A learner cannot remember 7 times 6. Show two ways to work it out from facts they do know.
questions.expected_answer: Start from 7 times 5, which is 35, and add one more 7 to get 42. Or start from 7 times 3, which is 21, and double it to get 42, because 6 is double 3.
